invariants: Automatic cleanup is confined to owned .goose/out paths without symlink/reparse traversal.
Delete only direct completed pytest test directories receipt.json/extracted.json with exact fake portable.zip bytes and explicit synthetic runtime marker or negative runtime fixture.
Retain real ZIPs,inputs,XML,logs,Source/browser observations,unknown files,active/interrupted workspaces and failed-test diagnostics.
Audit before deletion with fresh byte/hash validation and bounded examples;keep the newest two completed classified cleanup manifests.
Actual production pytest_sessionfinish runs only for normal completed pass/fail status;gate startup prunes only independently completed prior/focused runs.

Gate interruption retires the owned process tree before moving its workspace;retention errors cannot hide the primary failure. Expanded whole-suite budget is explicitly2800 seconds;individual deadlines and Source criteria remain unchanged.
identity: Owned literal absolute paths,exact synthetic archive bytes and revalidated size/SHA256 determine deletion candidates.
ownership: User explicitly authorized ongoing cleanup of expired reconstructible .goose/out process results;no external path or alias is owned.
ordering: Classify all candidates,audit planned state,revalidate immediately before unlink,then record completed or partial failed counts.
errors: Changed files refuse removal and retain partial audit. Unknown/malformed historical data stays retained. No cleanup hides original test failure.
cancellation: Interrupted/internal-error/not-run pytest statuses are preserved;active execution paths and incomplete XML/log are excluded.
adaptation: Independent repository maintenance,not upstream parity. Standard library and native literal extended Windows paths remain Python3.8/Win7 compatible.
open_questions: Immutable real acceptance/rejection evidence and unclassified research artifacts are retained;this does not authorize blanket removal of .goose/out.
